name: sgs/mega-panel
title: SGS Mega Panel
description: The content container of an SGS mega menu — lives inside a sgs_mega_menu post. Owns ALL variant + colour-scheme styling for its child sgs/mega-group and sgs/mega-aside blocks (parent-paints-child, CF-10): switching this block's style or colour scheme uniformly reshapes/recolours every group and aside inside it.

sgs._comment_mediaElements: 37-media-no-handroll remediation (2026-09-03). The aside's media is rendered by a CHILD block (sgs/mega-aside, parent-paints-child per CF-10) — this panel never renders an /

panel.label: Panel
panel._note: The `.sgs-mega-panel` root + its `.sgs-mega-panel__content` row (CF-12 pins groupGap onto this SAME element rather than a separate content element). Block-private (containerMirror:false, D294 deviation — this composite uses no SGS_Container_Wrapper grid/section machinery of its own; it hand-rolls its own flex/grid content-row per `style`, mirroring the wrapper's fill/box capability only). variant/style/colourScheme/accent/headings/bgBlur are variant-selector + arrangement-mode attrs, not css: property mappings, so they are deliberately absent from attrMap — they select WHICH scoped rule applies, per CF-4 (warn-only advisory, not global GAP-0). Column COUNT is no longer a separate attribute (dropped, QC-fix 2026-07-24) — the panel accepts a flexible 1-N sgs/mega-group children (add/remove/reorder), so the number of columns IS the number of groups. group-heading/link/desc/marker are CHILD-OWNED (sgs/heading, sgs/icon-list — HC2) and are declared on THOSE blocks' own manifests, not repeated here, even though this panel's CSS paints their colour/shape uniformly (CF-10).

aside.label: Aside slot
aside._note: The optional `.sgs-mega-aside` grid column, when a sgs/mega-aside child is present (asideSeparator's border-left divider is a compound value — colour+width+style — so it is documented here rather than mapped to a single css: key).

icon.label: Icon chip
icon._note: CROSS-BLOCK REUSE (2026-08-28, NULL css_element fix proposal §5): the actual rendered selector is `.sgs-icon-list__icon` — a CHILD block's (sgs/icon-list) own BEM class, reused here as markup inside this panel's parent-paints-child model (CF-10, see the `panel` element's own note). This element exists so iconBackground/iconColour (the icon-chip background-color/color painted uniformly across all 3 group styles — columns/cards/minimal, render.php §4) classify to a real owning element instead of drifting to NULL css_element, matching the same cross-block-reuse documentation pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase (e.g. how a composite documents a child-owned selector it paints but does not declare controls for). iconColourGradient (mega-panel.iconColour gradient-conformance close-out) is the sibling gradient attribute — added to this attrMap so it classifies to the SAME `icon` element instead of drifting ORPHAN:UNCLASSIFIED, matching `panel`/`group`'s own css:border-color-gradient siblings above.

group.label: Group tile
group._note: Targets `.sgs-mega-group` (resting) and `.sgs-mega-group:hover, .sgs-mega-group:focus-within` (hover) — both scoped to the `cards` style's tile only (render.php §4 card hover-lift); `columns`/`minimal` styles render no group-tile border at all. RENAMED 2026-08-28 (NULL css_element fix proposal §5): accentBorderColour -> groupBorderColour, accentBorderColourGradient -> groupBorderColourGradient. Bean then ruled, same day, that a genuine RESTING-state border control should exist alongside the hover — the original code only ever had a hover/focus-within border with no resting equivalent (the resting border on `cards` came solely from the `panel` element's shared --sgs-mm-panel-border token). groupBorderColour/groupBorderColourGradient (this element's BASE attrMap) are the new resting pair, default empty string so a fresh instance renders no colour override at rest — the `cards` tile keeps its existing --sgs-mm-panel-border-derived border unchanged until an operator sets one. The just-renamed groupBorderColour/groupBorderColourGradient were immediately re-renamed a second time, same day, to groupBorderColourHover/groupBorderColourGradientHover (base name = resting, base+Hover = hover — this codebase's own convention, e.g. backgroundColourHover) to make room for the new resting pair without a naming clash. Both pairs keep the same paired css:border-color + css:border-color-gradient shape in a single attrMap entry, per this codebase's established gradient-override convention.

iconBackground._note: Renamed from `accentBackground` (2026-08-28, NULL css_element fix proposal §5) — split from the old single `accent` attribute (D643, Bean-ruled: one colour attribute secretly painting 4 unrelated CSS properties blocks the gradient rollout — each property needs its own control). Feeds the icon-chip `background-color` (via the derived `--sgs-mm-soft` 10% tint) across all 3 group styles. Default unchanged from the retired `accent` attribute so existing rendering is preserved exactly. The generic name matches the established codebase convention (attribute name = generic `<element><Property>Colour`, default = bare token slug) and closes a NULL css_element classification gap via the new `icon` manifest element below.

groupBorderColour._note: NEW resting-state border-colour control (2026-08-28, Bean-ruled) — added alongside the pre-existing hover-only pair, which is now renamed groupBorderColourHover/groupBorderColourGradientHover (see below and the `group` manifest element's own note for the full rename chain: accentBorderColour -> groupBorderColour -> groupBorderColourHover). Default empty string: renders NO colour override at rest, so a fresh instance keeps its existing --sgs-mm-panel-border-derived `cards`-style tile border (render.php §4) exactly as before this attribute existed. Feeds `border-color` on `.sgs-mega-group` (cards style only) via the `--sgs-mm-group-border-resting` custom property, with a `var(..., var(--sgs-mm-panel-border))` fallback chain so an unset value is behaviour-neutral.

groupBorderColourGradient.description: NEW resting-state gradient override (2026-08-28), paired with groupBorderColour above. Non-empty wins over groupBorderColour on the SAME resting `.sgs-mega-group` (cards style) border via a masked ::before ring (D636 border-gradient rollout) — independent of the hover pair's own groupBorderColourGradientHover.

groupBorderColourHover._note: Renamed from `groupBorderColour` (2026-08-28) — itself renamed from `accentBorderColour` earlier the same day (NULL css_element fix proposal §5), then renamed again to make room for the new resting groupBorderColour pair above once Bean ruled a genuine resting-state border should exist too. Split from the old single `accent` attribute (D643). Feeds `border-color` on the `cards` style's hover/focus-within state, and is STILL the default source colour for the aside separator's border-left (asideSeparator.colour still overrides) — that dependency reads the resolved `--sgs-mm-accent-border` custom property, unchanged by this rename. Default unchanged ('accent') across every name in the chain.

groupBorderColourGradientHover.description: Renamed from `groupBorderColourGradient` (2026-08-28) — itself renamed from `accentBorderColourGradient` earlier the same day. CSS gradient string painting the `cards` style's hover/focus-within border with a masked ::before ring instead of a flat colour (D636 border-gradient rollout). Non-empty wins over groupBorderColourHover on that hover/focus-within state only.

iconColour._note: Renamed from `accentTextColour` (2026-08-28, NULL css_element fix proposal §5) — split from the old single `accent` attribute (D643). Feeds the icon-chip `color` (icon glyph colour) across all 3 group styles. Default unchanged from the retired `accent` attribute. The generic name matches the established codebase convention and closes a NULL css_element classification gap via the new `icon` manifest element below.

iconColourGradient._note: Sibling gradient attribute (D636 text-colour/gradient pattern) for `iconColour` — closes the mega-panel.iconColour non-conformant colour row. A non-empty valid CSS gradient string wins over the flat `iconColour` on the icon-chip `color`, rendered via `sgs_text_colour_decl()`'s background-clip:text trio + its mandatory `sgs_text_colour_gradient_fallback_rule()` companion. `iconColour` itself is left completely untouched when this is set, matching every other flat/gradient sibling pair in this block (groupBorderColour/groupBorderColourGradient etc.).

accentBackgroundImage._note: Split from the old single `accent` attribute (D643). Feeds the aside's cursor-spotlight radial-gradient glow (`background`, i.e. a background-image, via the derived `--sgs-mm-soft-image` 10% tint) — only visible when `data-spotlight` is active (view.js, §6 U6). Default unchanged from the retired `accent` attribute.

panelPadding._note: BOX-object shape (top/right/bottom/left per tier) — NOT a scalar. render.php emits this through sgs_emit_responsive_css() with 'box' => true, which reads the four sides; the previous scalar default ({desktop:'28px'}) produced NO padding at all, so the panel rendered flush to its own border and both group headings touched the top/left edge (Bean's eye, 2026-07-28). Classic STOP-D328: the declared SHAPE must match what the consumer expects, or the value is silently dropped. Matches sgs/mega-aside's asidePadding shape exactly.

borderWidth._note: B4 (2026-09-04) — SgsBorderControl migration. Empty object = unset; render.php falls back to 1px on every side so a pre-existing instance (which never wrote this attr) keeps its exact current 1px-solid hairline unchanged. Base tier only per SgsBorderControl's own contract (D294 2026-08-29: per-device border width has no real use case).

borderStyle._note: B4 (2026-09-04) — paired with borderWidth above. Default 'solid' matches the pre-migration hardcoded `border:1px solid` shorthand, so a fresh/existing instance renders identically.

brandsEyebrow._note: brands-variant only — a small mono eyebrow label rendered above the logo grid (§3). Deliberately a scalar panel attribute rather than a child block: the brands variant's content (sgs/card-grid + sgs/mega-aside) has no wrapper block available to host a heading ABOVE just the grid (mega-group is locked to heading+icon-list, out of scope to modify), so the panel renders this text itself, spanning the full content row rather than just the left column — a documented deviation from §3's 'left flex:1: eyebrow + grid' framing.

staggerOnOpen._note: Opt-in staggered-reveal on panel open (§6 U4) — maps to the `data-stagger` attribute the shared stagger effect module watches for. Off by default; the disclosure module (owned separately) is what actually toggles the panel open/closed.

viewAllPlacement._note: Where the menu item's own destination link ("View all X") sits INSIDE this panel. CF-15 requires that link to exist somewhere reachable — the trigger is a <button>, so without it the item's page is unreachable from the nav and invisible to crawlers — but WHERE it sits is an operator choice, never hard-wired (Bean 2026-07-28). `auto` = show it only when this panel has no CTA button of its own (so a panel whose aside already links there stays clean); `none` = never; `bottom-left`/`bottom-right` = always, in that corner of the panel's footer row. ENUM DECLARED 2026-08-06 (Spec 35 A2), REVERSING this note's previous 'NO JSON enum — PHP-validated (blockjson-enum-coerces-invalid-to-default)' clause. That reasoning does not hold for THIS attribute, measured: block.json default is 'auto', render.php:534's in_array fallback is ALSO 'auto', and the allow-list at :532 is these same four values — so WP's out-of-enum coercion and the PHP fallback produce an IDENTICAL result for every possible stored value. The declaration is therefore behaviour-neutral, and buys three things: the row classifies via the existing tested TIER 3.5 to role `enum-mode`, WP validates the value, and the client gets a real select control instead of a free-text box (Spec 35 Part B). Same argument D456 used to ADD an enum to sgs/site-header-row.layout, treating coercion as a safety net rather than a hazard. RESIDUAL RISK, named rather than hidden: if the PHP allow-list at :532 ever gains a value and this enum is not updated in the same commit, WP will silently coerce the new value to 'auto'. That is a DRIFT hazard, not a coercion hazard — the inverse of what Detector 8 already checks (it finds PHP allow-lists with NO block.json enum).
